artifact_inventory.description: Standalone exact-integer scan of all arithmetic-progression parameters 1 <= d < x <= 3000, checking integer area and the predicted two-prime-support family.
Deterministic output of the bounded check: 4,498,500 parameter pairs, 6,434 Heronian pairs, 44 two-prime-support hits, and zero mismatches.

limitations: The theorem is specific to side lengths in arithmetic progression and does not classify arbitrary Heronian triangles or HAP areas with three or more distinct prime divisors. Originality is to the best of our knowledge. The full text of Read (2025), On HAP triangles, was not inspected; only the publisher extract and references were available, leaving a concrete residual overlap risk.
record_title: Minimal prime support in arithmetic-progression Heronian triangles
scientific_context: A Heronian triangle with integer sides in nonconstant arithmetic progression has area with exactly two distinct prime divisors if and only if it is (3t,4t,5t) with t=2^u3^v; equivalently, (3,4,5) is the unique primitive case of minimal area-prime support.
